# Dependencies and install order

This page is for developers who write the `<requires>` of a site package, and for administrators who wonder why an
install fetched, replaced or refused a package. It answers: how a requirement is written, how it is checked, and in
which order packages are fetched and installed.

2. [How min-version is compared](#how-min-version-is-compared)
3. [Fetching: what the wizard downloads](#fetching-what-the-wizard-downloads)
4. [Installing: the order on the site](#installing-the-order-on-the-site)
5. [Requirements of requirements](#requirements-of-requirements)

7. [Checklist for your own requirements](#checklist-for-your-own-requirements)

## How a requirement is written

```xml
<dependencies>
  <requires>
    <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_classes" min-version="5.1" />
    <require type="ezpackage" name="sevenx_multisite_democontent" min-version="5.1" />
  </requires>
</dependencies>
```

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `ezpackage` for another package. The Create sites step ignores any other type |
| `name` | The `<name>` of the required package, which is also its file name on the package server |
| `min-version` | The lowest `<number>-<release>` that satisfies the requirement; without it, any version does |

The order of the `<require>` elements is the order of installation. Put content classes before the content that
uses them, as `sevenx_multisite` does.

## How min-version is compared

A package's version is `eZPackage::getVersion()`: `<version><number>` and `<version><release>` joined by `-`. It is
compared with `min-version` by `eZPackageVersion::compareFull()` (`kernel/classes/ezpackageversion.php`):

- The part after the last `-` is the release number only when it is all digits; the rest is the version number.
- Version numbers compare by Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence. Older forms are read too: `1` and `1.0` read as
  `1.0.0`, a fourth part compares after PATCH, `3.4.0beta1` reads as the prerelease `beta1`.
- When the version numbers are equal, the release numbers compare as numbers (a missing one counts as 0).

| Installed | `min-version` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `6.0-10-stable` (`sevenx_classes` in 6.0.15) | `5.1` | satisfied: 6 is greater than 5 |
| `1.0-1` | `1.0-2` | not satisfied |
| `1.0-1` | `1.0.0-1` | satisfied: equal |

> **Note**
> The `version` attribute of an `index.xml` entry is not compared with `min-version`. Only the version inside an
> imported package counts.

## Fetching: what the wizard downloads

`eZStepSiteTypes::downloadDependantPackages()` (`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`) runs after the site
package is imported. For every `<require>` of the site package, in order:

1. Look for a package of that name in the local repository.
2. If it exists and `compareFull( installed, min-version ) >= 0`: keep it, download nothing.
3. If it exists but is older: remove it from the repository and download the new one.
4. If it does not exist: download it.
5. To download, look the name up in the index; the URL is the entry's `url`. A name the index does not list stops
   the step with "Download of package '...' failed. You may upload the package manually."

Each download is imported with `eZPackage::import()` into the repository its vendor names. In a kickstarter dry run
everything is downloaded into the temporary repository `var/storage/packages/dryrun` instead, so the whole chain is
checked without touching the real repository.

## Installing: the order on the site

The Create sites step (`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php`) then:

1. Fetches the site package; error `EZSW-041` when it cannot.
2. Includes its install scripts and calls `eZSitePreInstall()` (see
   [Install scripts in a site package](install-scripts-in-a-site-package.md)).
3. Walks the site package's `<require>` list in order. For each `type="ezpackage"` item:
   - fetches the package; error `EZSW-050` "Could not fetch required package" when it is missing;
   - when its `install_type` is `install`, installs it; error `EZSW-051` "Unable to install package" when that
     fails;
   - when its `install_type` is `import`, leaves it as it is (a site style, for example, whose files the installer
     scripts use).
4. Writes the settings, roles and preferences, and calls `eZSitePostInstall()`.

For `sevenx_multisite` this means: `sevenx_classes` is installed first, then `sevenx_multisite_democontent`, then the
installer runs.

## Requirements of requirements

`eZPackage::install()` handles requirements too, like a package manager: before it installs a package's own items,
it installs every package that package requires, one level after another
(`eZPackage::installUnaudited()`, "apt-like: pre-install all required packages"). A package already being installed
higher up the chain is skipped, so a loop does not run for ever. A required package that is not in the repository
only logs a warning there.

> **Note**
> From 6.0.15 on the setup wizard **downloads** the whole chain: the site package's requirements, theirs, and so on,
> each package once (`eZStepSiteTypes::downloadDependantPackages()`), from any package server it reads. Before, it
> downloaded only the direct requirements, and a requirement's own requirements had to be in the local repository
> already, or they were only logged as missing when it was installed. Listing every package a site needs in the
> site package itself, as every site package of the 6.0.15 index does, still works with older releases.

`eZPackage::install()` does not check whether a package is installed already: when two requirements require the
same package, its items run twice. The kernel only drops repeated items inside one package.

## The other dependency sections

`<provides>`, `<obsoletes>` and `<conflicts>` are read and kept, and shown by the package pages and `ezpm info`, but
neither the setup steps nor `eZPackage::install()` act on them. The 7x design packages declare
`<provide type="ezfile" name="collection" value="default"/>` for information.

## Checklist for your own requirements

- [ ] Every package the site needs is listed in the site package itself, with `type="ezpackage"`.
- [ ] Classes come before content, extensions before content that uses their datatypes.
- [ ] Every `name` is listed in the `index.xml` the installation reads.
- [ ] `min-version` is at most the version inside the archive on the server.
- [ ] The required packages that must change the site have `install_type="install"`.
